title: Uncommitted: a DELETE without WHERE is still open in a colleague's session

Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: ROLLBACK TRANSACTION 'erase[s] all data modifications made from the start of the transaction' and 'also frees the resources held by the transaction'; 'A transaction can't be rolled back after a COMMIT TRANSACTION statement is executed'. That a DELETE without WHERE affects every row and that the open transaction's locks block the foreign key check of inserted orders (Azure SQL Database reads under read committed snapshot are not blocked, but foreign key validation takes locks) are to verify against the DELETE and locking pages.

brief.situation: You are a junior data analyst at Corvin Garden Supply, a fictional retailer, with rights to the Azure SQL database shop. A colleague, Jo, meant to delete one test customer and ran BEGIN TRANSACTION; DELETE FROM Customers; then left for a meeting with the query window open. New orders, whose foreign key to Customers must be checked on insert, have been waiting since 09:14. The 10:00 garden-center opening brings most of the day's online orders.
handover: Jo's query window is still connected; Jo has given you the laptop and said 'do what is right'.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows Jo's open transaction, the Customers table and the orders waiting on it.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: what Jo's statement did, what you ran, and why not COMMIT.

parts.label: Did
parts.modelAnswer: DELETE FROM Customers had no WHERE clause, so it removed all 18,240 rows, inside a transaction that was never committed. Its locks blocked the order queries.

parts.label: Ran
parts.modelAnswer: ROLLBACK TRANSACTION undid the delete and released the locks; DELETE ... WHERE CustomerID = 90001 removed only the test customer.

parts.label: Not commit
parts.modelAnswer: COMMIT would have made the mistake permanent. Until then it could be undone.

expertPath.text: DELETE with no WHERE in an open transaction; count 0 and @@TRANCOUNT 1; orders wait on Jo's session; test row is 90001.

committed.headline: Uncommitted means undoable
committed.body: While a transaction is open, ROLLBACK undoes it. COMMIT makes it permanent. Releasing locks the wrong way turned a near miss into data loss.

openingBlocked.headline: An open transaction blocks others
openingBlocked.body: Until a transaction ends, its locks stay. Here the right ending is ROLLBACK.

rolledBack.headline: Good: read before you end it
rolledBack.body: You read the statement and the open transaction, rolled back instead of committing, ran the correct DELETE with a WHERE, checked the count, and shared a habit that prevents it.

scoring.modelReasoning: The DELETE had no WHERE, so it removed every customer, but the transaction is still open: nothing is final, and its locks block orders. Roll it back, which undoes the delete and releases the locks, then delete only the test customer with a WHERE clause and check. COMMIT would make the loss permanent; reopening your own window changes nothing.
